title: POC weekly sync - app integration (SDK, tool/function calls, structured output)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review SDK integration progress, results from last week's tool/function calling tests, and structured output schema. Decided to change SDK flow to emit explicit tool call metadata and agreed next steps for latency benchmarks and updated examples.
topics: structured output schema for downstream ingestion
next_steps: Leah to publish updated SDK snippet with tool-calling example and structured output by 2025-10-24
BlueStream to run end-to-end latency test and share logs by 2025-10-28
Carlos to send security docs (SOC2 + KMS integration notes) today
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on private deployment options for 2025-11-04
action_items: Leah: update SDK example to include function/tool call and structured JSON response schema - due 2025-10-24
Marcus: run end-to-end latency test (3 scenarios: hosted, dedicated baseline, cached) and upload logs - due 2025-10-28
Carlos: email SOC2 summary + KMS/HSM integration note and dataset redaction guide - due 2025-10-21 (EOD)
Priya: confirm success criteria for structured output (fields + validation rules) - due 2025-10-23
transcript: [00:00] Carlos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we've got about 37 minutes on the calendar. quick roll call?
[00:08] Anita: Hi this is Anita, CTO at BlueStream. thanks Carlos, Marcus and Priya are on from our side.
[00:13] Marcus: Marcus here, lead engineer. morning all.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, PM - hi!
[00:20] Carlos: Great. Leah from our infra/team will cover the SDK changes. Leah you want to kick off with what you shipped last night?

[00:30] Leah: Yeah, sure. So I pushed an update to the SDK that adds a first-class helper for function/tool calling; it's basically a wrapper that captures tool metadata (tool_name, args, confidence) and serializes it alongside the main text response as a structured JSON block. The idea is to make downstream ingestion easier for BlueStream's pipeline.
[01:05] Marcus: Nice. Does that preserve streaming so we can still show partial tokens in the UI?

[01:12] Leah: Yes — streaming still works, we emit an interleaved event for the "tool_call" when it happens and then resume the text stream. There's a little bit of buffering for the tool payload to ensure schema integrity but it's sub-100ms in most cases.
[01:35] Priya: that buffering, will it change our perceived latency? We care about first-byte for user experience.

[01:42] Leah: Good question. For first-byte the impact is negligible for normal text-only responses. For a request that triggers a tool call immediately, you see the tool-call event after the initial tokens, so maybe a 50-150ms delta depending on network. We can optimize with prefix caching so that downstream calls are faster — that's on our optimize roadmap.

[02:10] Anita: We ran the quick integration yesterday and saw two odd things: 1) the tool_name got transcribed as 'searcher' in one call, which is weird, and 2) the structured payload came back with a camelCase/ snake_case mix which breaks our validator.

[02:28] Leah: hmm yeah there are a couple of transposition issues — this is likely the auto-serializer mixing conventions. I can make the SDK normalize to a strict snake_case (or whatever you prefer) before emitting. On the tool_name mislabel, that sounds like a model output issue where the model paraphrased the tool name, we run a post-hoc mapping to canonical tool ids but we should tighten that mapping.
[02:50] Marcus: If the model paraphrases tool names, can we force the tool token to be a literal via the function-signature style? We tried something like that but it didn't always stick.

[02:58] Leah: We have two options: embed a hard-coded function signature in the prompt so model returns a canonical name, or enforce the canonicalization client-side by matching synonyms. I recommend doing both for robustness — add a function signature and then canonicalize on receipt.
[03:20] Carlos: Quick ask on security — are any of these tool call args being logged in Redwood's hosted logs? BlueStream is concerned about PII.

[03:28] Leah: By default we log metadata but not full args. For POCs we can enable redaction or disable logging of args altogether. We also support KMS-backed encryption for sensitive fields; I'll include the KMS/HSM integration note in the docs I send after the call.
[03:45] Anita: That's important. Marcus, make sure our test payloads include a PII scenario so we validate redaction matches our compliance needs.
[03:53] Marcus: will do.
[04:00] Priya: about structured output: we need a stable schema for the downstream ETL. Leah, can you show the example schema you mentioned?

[04:10] Leah: Sure — I have a snippet. (screen share stutters) ok reading out: {"event_type":"tool_call","tool": {"id":"string","name":"string"},"result": {"status":"string","payload":"string"},"confidence": 0.0} — so basic shape. we can add an outputs array for multi-step tool interactions.

[04:40] Marcus: That confidence field is useful. For us we need a top-level "action" field and then strong typing for payload — like an object schema. Right now the SDK example has payload as free string and that breaks our JSON schema enforcement.
[04:55] Leah: Ok we can push a stricter typed payload in the SDK and optional JSON-schema validation step client-side. I'll attach a JSON Schema file in the PR.
[05:10] Carlos: Can you also make the SDK emit a separate 'events' stream so your pipeline can subscribe only to tool events and ignore conversational tokens?

[05:18] Leah: yes that's the current plan — there's an events websocket or webhook option; for hosted API we have server-sent events and webhooks. For private deployments we can mirror events to your internal kinesis/ pubsub.

[05:35] Anita: We are leaning away from hosted for PHI reasons, but we want to validate integration first. this POC is to evaluate both UX and performance so the hosted run is ok for now as long as logs are redacted.
[05:48] Carlos: Good call. On performance, Marcus you ran the quick benchmarks last night — can you summarize?

[05:55] Marcus: Yeah we ran three tests: 1) hosted default (no caching), 2) hosted with prefix cache enabled, 3) dedicated small pool. Median token latency for a typical prompt was 120ms hosted, 90ms with caching, and 85ms on dedicated. Cold start for the tool call path added about 180-230ms in some runs because of kernel selection overhead.

[06:25] Leah: those cold-start numbers sound higher than expected — are you sending long sequence prompts? Kernel selection overhead is dependent on sequence length and quantization. We can force a warm-up sequence to reduce cold starts in the POC.
[06:38] Marcus: Mostly short prompts, but we did include a 1k prefix in one scenario. I'll share the exact logs in the artifact link (we'll drop to the shared drive).
[06:48] Priya: is there an obvious tuning parameter to reduce the tool call overhead? batching? kernel pinning?

[06:54] Leah: Batching helps for throughput but not single-request latency. For single-request latency you can: 1) use a smaller model variant for tool calls, 2) enable KV cache priming so model doesn't redo prefix work, 3) use dedicated pool with pre-warmed instances. We can also return a lightweight tool token that defers heavy compute to an async worker if your UX allows it.
[07:20] Anita: I like the pre-warm approach for the dedicated runs. For our legal team we need clear SLAs in the next phase if we go dedicated.
[07:28] Carlos: We can provide an SLA template. Leah will follow up on the exact warm-up scripts.
[07:33] Leah: I'll attach warm-up scripts and an example autoscaler policy. the script pings generate calls to keep kernels hot and primes KV caches.
[07:43] Marcus: Another wrinkle we saw: structured responses sometimes include trailing commentary text after the JSON block which breaks our parser. Is there a recommended delimiter?

[07:52] Leah: We support a 'json_only' mode where the model is instructed to emit only the JSON payload. It isn't perfect but combined with the function signature and a post-processor that extracts the first JSON block it's robust. We'll enforce that in the SDK example.

[08:10] Priya: Great. For our acceptance criteria, we need the structured output to validate 95% of mock inputs and first-byte latency under 200ms for typical queries. I'll formalize that and send it to Carlos.

[08:22] Carlos: sounds good. quick note on instrumentation: make sure your client is surfacing token-level cost and latency metrics — Redwood console can show per-route but you should instrument in-app for end-to-end numbers.
[08:36] Marcus: we'll add client-side instrumentation. any recommendations on sampling? full trace for 10% and aggregated metrics otherwise?
[08:44] Leah: 10% sampling plus error-triggered full traces is a good start.
[08:50] Anita: back to security briefly — can we get a list of what Redwood logs by default and what can be disabled?

[08:58] Carlos: I'll send that in the docs pack; basically: request metadata, latency, model, and non-arg metadata by default. args and full payloads are opt-in and can be redacted. we also support customer-managed encryption keys.
[09:12] Marcus: ok thanks. one more technical: when a tool call triggers multiple sub-tools (e.g. search -> db lookup), does the SDK flatten that into one event or emit a sequence?
[09:22] Leah: We emit an events array so you get a sequence with parent-child relationships preserved; each event has an id and parent_id.
[09:31] Priya: that's perfect for our ETL.

[09:35] Carlos: Alright let's confirm the immediate next steps. Leah, you'll publish SDK changes and JSON Schema; Marcus will run the latency tests and upload logs; Carlos will send security docs; Priya will confirm acceptance criteria. Anything else?
[09:49] Priya: can we also get a short demo of the webhook/events flow next week?
[09:54] Carlos: yes let's schedule a webhook demo - how's 2025-11-04 for folks?
[09:59] Anita: works for me.
[10:02] Marcus: works.
[10:05] Carlos: Great. I'll book it. ok we'll wrap up — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the doc links and Leah will open the PR for the SDK examples.
[10:16] Leah: thanks all, bye.
[10:18] Anita: thanks, bye.
